corrected_value.title: Impact of a mentoring and skills group program on mental health outcomes for maltreated children in foster care.

decisions.quote: Fostering Healthy Futures (FHF) is a preventive PYD intervention for preadolescent children who have experienced maltreatment and placement in out-of-home care. It consists of individualized mentoring and weekly skills groups for 30 weeks. The conceptual and theoretical basis for FHF and anticipated proximal and distal effects are delineated elsewhere (cf. Taussig, Culhane & Hettleman, 2007 ). A pilot RCT with 156 youth found positive impacts on multi-informant (child, caregiver, teacher) reports of mental health functioning (including trauma symptoms), mental health services, and quality of life ( Taussig & Culhane, 2010 ).
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly aims to replicate and extend the mental health findings of the pilot FHF RCT cited as Taussig & Culhane (2010) (DOI: 10.1001/archpediatrics.2010.124) in the text and reference list. The shipped row pointed to an uncited 2012 conference abstract (Taussig, 2012; 10.1037/e522512014-027) instead of the cited primary published trial article.

decisions.quote: Intervention youth scored significantly lower on the mental health index ( β = −.11; t = −2.32; p < .05), posttraumatic stress symptoms ( β = −.09; t = −2.01; p < .05) and dissociation scales ( β = −.12; t = −2.76; p < .01), and they were less likely to be receiving mental health treatment at T2 (B = −.47; Wald = 4.43; p =.04). Intervention and control groups did not differ on quality of life or psychotropic medication use.
decisions.reason: Resolving the dependent original identity to Taussig & Culhane (2010), the paper states that the pilot RCT found positive impacts on three domains: multi-informant mental health functioning (including trauma symptoms), mental health services, and quality of life. In the replication, FHF significantly reduced mental health problems (mental health index, posttraumatic stress, and dissociation) and mental health treatment utilization, confirming the first two pilot findings, but found no main effect difference between intervention and control groups on quality of life. Because the Discussion confirms the specific effects on mental health symptomatology and service utilization rather than stating an overall replication verdict that all pilot findings held, codebook Rule 2 governs and the mix of confirmed and unconfirmed original findings yields 'mixed'.

decisions.quote: The current study sought to replicate and extend the mental health findings of the pilot FHF trial by adding data from five additional cohorts ( N =270) as well as examine moderating effects.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding agree that the study is a replication: it collected new data from five additional cohorts (N = 270) pooled with the five pilot cohorts to re-test the published mental health findings of the pilot FHF trial (Taussig & Culhane, 2010).

corrected_value.title: The moderating effect of risk exposure on an efficacious intervention for maltreated children.

decisions.location: Introduction, Current Study, Results (Moderating Analyses), Discussion, and References, line 1
decisions.quote: In the FHF pilot study we found that (1) severity of neglect did not moderate outcomes, suggesting that children with severe neglect histories were just as likely to benefit from the intervention as those with less severe neglect histories ( Taussig, Culhane, Garrido, Knudtson, & Petrenko, 2013 ) but that (2) level of risk (i.e., exposure to ACEs) did moderate some outcomes (i.e., posttraumatic stress and dissociative symptoms), such that maltreated children exposed to a relatively higher number of ACEs did not experience the same reduction in trauma symptoms as children exposed to fewer adversities ( Weiler & Taussig, 2017 ).
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work. Weiler & Taussig (2017) (10.1080/15374416.2017.1295379, Journal of Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology) is a distinct 2017 study reporting that baseline exposure to adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) moderated FHF intervention effects on trauma symptoms such that youth with fewer ACEs experienced stronger reductions in posttraumatic stress symptoms. In the Current Study section, the authors formulate their sole directional a priori moderation hypothesis specifically to retest this finding; in Moderating Analyses they test the ACEs x treatment interaction on T2 outcomes; and in Discussion they explicitly state that their results 'replicated our earlier finding that children exposed to relatively fewer ACEs tended to benefit more on some outcomes (i.e., posttraumatic stress symptoms and quality of life)'. Shipped row 754 (Taussig, 2012, 10.1037/e522512014-027) and target_index 0 (Taussig & Culhane, 2010) predated this 2017 moderation study by 5 to 7 years and reported main RCT effects rather than the Weiler & Taussig (2017) ACEs moderation finding.

decisions.quote: The current study sought to replicate and extend the mental health findings of the pilot FHF trial by adding data from five additional cohorts ( N =270) as well as examine moderating effects. The study first examined FHF’s effects on key mental health outcomes: a multi-informant (child, caregiver, teacher) index of mental health problems, youth-reported posttraumatic stress symptoms (including dissociation), youth-reported quality of life, and caregiver- and youth-reported use of mental health treatment (including psychotropic medications).
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work. Although the replication paper cites Taussig & Culhane (2010) (10.1001/archpediatrics.2010.124) for the main mental health findings of the Fostering Healthy Futures (FHF) pilot RCT on preadolescent youth in out-of-home care, the Method section establishes that there was only one prior FHF RCT on preadolescent youth in out-of-home care (the 5-cohort pilot trial recruited from 2002 to 2006, N = 156) before the 5 additional efficacy cohorts were combined in the current paper. Shipped row input_row_index 754 (10.1037/e522512014-027, Taussig, 2012, 'Fostering Healthy Futures: A Randomized Controlled Trial of an Intervention for Preadolescent Youth in Out-of-Home Care') is an alternate APA PsycEXTRA conference/grey-literature report of that same FHF pilot RCT. Because a conference/grey-literature record and full journal article represent the same original work, target_index 0 is already covered by shipped row 754.
